title: Anyone else making an MMO featuring LLMs?
author: enfarious
selftext:
So I started vibe coding an MMO to see how far that could get. I'd seen lots of folks insisting that large scale projects just fail. I seem to be doing okay so far. 



Anyone else?

comments.author: n3wdl
comments.body: How far is you progress currently?

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: I have a server and 2 diff clients, multiple logins handled, chat, party, npcs, mobs, wildlife, weather, few other things otw

replies.author: n3wdl
replies.body: Sounds very nice, i love weather and wildlife that creates atmosphere.  What type of combat?

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: A mix of TSW and FFXI is the best description I can give. Tab targeting, limited action sets, more about coordination and strat than about mashing the perfect rotation until it ends.

comments.author: addictedtosoda
comments.body: I started with a text based RPG and am about to start.

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: I did a MOO first, it was super fun.

replies.author: addictedtosoda
replies.body: I did decide to shift and make my game into a book creation engine though.

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: Oh, that could be really fun too. Choose your own adventure books or just straight novel?

replies.author: addictedtosoda
replies.body:
You create your world by doing it manually, uploading what you’re already working on, or choosing one of 19 separate starting points/povs 

Then you play a choose your own adventure game

After 20 events from the game you can create a book outline or keep going 

The book creation uses the world bible which is build from what you created and then goes through a special pipeline I created.

And then you publish on the site bookstore, mark whether you want to let people play in your world and then you profit if they make a book too

comments.author: Time_Series4689
comments.body: What's your tech stack? Isn't the main problem costs by scaling?

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body:
I'm not up to worrying about scale yet. I just wanted to see if I could make a playable game. So far it's still working.

**Server**

* **Runtime**: Node.js (≥20) + TypeScript
* **Framework**: Express + [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) (WebSocket-based real-time comms)
* **Database**: PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM
* **Cache/Messaging**: Redis (ioredis) — pub/sub for distributed zone servers
* **Auth**: Passport + OpenID Connect, JWT, bcrypt
* **AI/LLM**: OpenAI-compatible API (pointed at LMStudio locally via `openai` SDK), plus Anthropic SDK
* **Logging**: Pino
* **Validation**: Zod
* **Architecture**: Gateway + distributed Zone Servers (can run monolithic or split)

**Web Client**

* **Build**: Vite + TypeScript
* **3D**: Three.js
* **Networking**: [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) client
* **Map**: Leaflet (for the corruption/ward map overlay)

**Infrastructure**

* PostgreSQL for persistent state
* Redis for inter-server messaging and session coordination
* LMStudio running locally for LLM (companion AI, behavior trees, NPC engagement)

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: Thanks I'm gonna give this a look.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Not a fully blown mmo but I tried making a rpg and these are the issues I ran into:

- AIs can't really generate good animations for rigs (haven't checked recently but i tried a few ai animation tools)
- AIs can't really generate game maps 
- AIs can generate game icons but it is not a quick process

I think AI can save you time but it is still going to be time consuming; personally I think it will take me months to a year even if all the assets are generated properly for me to use

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: Yeah I have zero for assets still. As I creep up on I want something to look at cause the rules are about done I started thinking those pipelines are gonna be work all over again. The server is nearly complete though and a text based client (cause I came up on MUDs and MOOs lol) and a graphical one, for testing.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: Ai powered text based game is a proven path at this point. Good luck

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: Yeah I already did a MOO. This is to see if I can take it all the way with a proper 3D client as well. It's fun as hell.

replies.author: acexprt
replies.body: This is where scaling down to 2D to prove out your game concept comes in handy. 3D is a handful and can get complex real fast. Doing it in 2D where AI can generate sprites, sprite sheets, textures is the easiest way to test a concept. I personally love Google Flow for making textures and sprites because it can keep it all in the same style. Another pro tip, have AI make you a map builder or other tools to help you create. Build your own sprite sheet maker. I have a backend mission generator that is similar to Arma3 mission editor so I can build the missions for my game. No need to have it all done in code when I can make a UI. Work smarter not harder.

comments.author: SproutsJeremy
comments.body:
I started with a text based rpg. All the procedural systems are made to be able to generate large scale worlds with dozens of towns and cities, tens of thousands of npcs, one day, definitely no time soon lol. 

As I’m coming close to completion of my game, I’ve changed the game idea about 6 times in the past month. I’m convinced getting from 95% to 100% is the hardest part lmao

replies.author: enfarious
replies.body: I love the sound of that, a proper world generator. That could make for some really fun replay.

comments.body: I’ve started a multiplayer 2D air combat game that has RTS elements. It’s been a ton of work but seeing results and setting weekly/daily goals has been helpful. I’m about 3 weeks in at this point.

replies.body: Nice. I'd love to see your progress if you want to share. Mine's on github.
